title: SmartNIC Data Exchange Framework
problem: HPC systems require efficient mechanisms to gather and exchange arbitrary host data from distributed nodes. Smart Network Interface Cards (SmartNICs) present an underutilized opportunity to offload data exchange operations with minimal system overhead.
motivation: As HPC systems grow larger, in-network data processing via SmartNICs can reduce CPU burden, lower latency, and enable novel system management and monitoring capabilities without traditional network stack overhead.
method: Develop a novel SmartNIC-based data exchange framework supporting three different data exchange methods. Characterize latency, throughput, and performance scaling under different framework configurations on real HPC hardware.
key_novelty: Novel SmartNIC data exchange framework leveraging in-network processing for arbitrary host data gathering; evaluation of multiple exchange methodologies and their latency/throughput trade-offs.
contributions: SmartNIC-based data exchange framework for HPC systems
Support for three distinct data exchange methods with configurable trade-offs
Characterization of framework latency and performance across configurations
Demonstration of minimal system overhead compared to traditional approaches
limitations: Limited details on specific configurations and methodologies in abstract; scalability evaluation scope not fully clear; comparison with other SmartNIC approaches not discussed.
